statement:
Let \(\tfrac{1}{2} \leq a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n \leq 5\) and let \(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n\) satisfy \(4x_i^2 - 4a_i x_i + (a_i-1)^2 \leq 0\). Prove that
\[\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2}{n}} \leq \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}{n} + 1.\]

Let \(R, r\) be the circumradius and inradius of a regular 1986-gonal pyramid. Prove that \(\dfrac{R}{r} \geq 1 + \dfrac{1}{\cos\frac{\pi}{1986}}\), and find the total surface area of the pyramid when equality holds.
Suppose \(M(y)\) is a polynomial of degree \(n\) such that \(M(y) = 2^y\) for \(y = 1, 2, \ldots, n+1\). Compute \(M(n+2)\).

Let \(ABCD\) be a square of side \(2a\). An equilateral triangle \(AMB\) is constructed in the plane through \(AB\) perpendicular to the square. Point \(S\) moves on \(AB\) with \(SB = x\). Let \(P\) be the projection of \(M\) on \(SC\), and \(E, O\) the midpoints of \(AB\) and \(CM\).\\
a) Find the locus of \(P\) as \(S\) moves on \(AB\).\\
b) Find the maximum and minimum lengths of \(SO\).

Find all \(n > 1\) such that
\[\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2 \geq x_n \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} x_i\]
holds for all real numbers \(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n\).

A sequence of positive integers is constructed as follows: the first term is 1; the next two terms are 2, 4; the next three terms are 5, 7, 9; the next four terms are 10, 12, 14, 16; and so on. Find the \(n\)-th term of the sequence.
